country.comment: Empirical analysis covers municipalities in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil, within the context of Brazil's national sanitation regulatory framework.
country.where_found: PDF p. 10, Section 1; PDF p. 16, Section 3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative cross-sectional OLS regression with White-corrected robust standard errors using four PCA/varimax institutional capacity factor scores (78.51% total variance explained). Descriptive statistics also show that only 59.8% of reporting municipalities (N = 456) had a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan (PMSB) and 50.9% (N = 471) had a Municipal Basic Sanitation Policy (PPSB), mandatory under Law 11.445/2007 for federal funding, with smaller municipalities having significantly lower adoption (chi-square p < 0.05).
effect_estimate.value: In robust multiple linear regressions across N = 391 municipalities in Minas Gerais, institutional capacity factor scores significantly predicted service coverage: (1) Water supply coverage (mean 61.608%; R² = 0.1601, F = 16.82, p = 0.000): Financial Capacity β = 6.015 (SE = 1.020, p < 0.001), Technical Capacity β = 2.669 (SE = 0.985, p = 0.007), Operational Capacity β = 2.412 (SE = 0.916, p = 0.009), Political Capacity [existence of Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan PMSB and Policy PPSB under Law 11.445/2007] β = -1.890 (SE = 0.883, p = 0.033); (2) Sanitary sewage coverage (mean 42.347%; R² = 0.1933, F = 24.90, p = 0.000): Financial Capacity β = 7.359 (SE = 1.482, p < 0.001), Technical Capacity β = 3.941 (SE = 1.574, p = 0.013), Operational Capacity β = 13.068 (SE = 1.650, p < 0.001), Political Capacity β = -0.661 (SE = 1.641, p = 0.687); (3) Household solid waste collection coverage (mean 47.883%; R² = 0.5667, F = 135.74, p = 0.000): Financial Capacity β = 10.064 (SE = 1.413, p < 0.001), Technical Capacity β = 2.249 (SE = 1.273, p = 0.078), Operational Capacity β = 28.260 (SE = 1.400, p < 0.001), Political Capacity β = 2.555 (SE = 1.329, p = 0.055).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 19, Section 4 & Table 2; PDF pp. 22-23, Section 4 & Tables 3-4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional municipal-level regression analysis (design ceiling <= 2) documenting statistical associations between municipal institutional capacity indices (including statutory planning/policy adoption under Law 11.445/2007, municipal technical staff, operational staffing/vehicles, and per-capita revenues/expenditures) and municipal water/sewage/waste coverage rates, without direct observation of administrative connection/delivery processes or quasi-experimental identification.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 17-19, Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF pp. 22-23, Section 4 & Table 4

mechanism_flags.comment: Empirically examines municipal adoption of mandatory Municipal Basic Sanitation Plans (PMSB) and Municipal Basic Sanitation Policies (PPSB) required under Law 11.445/2007 to access federal funds and validate contracts (ELIGIBILITY, planning, political_coordination), alongside municipal governance/technical capacity and intergovernmental fragmentation of responsibilities and resources across municipalities and state utilities under Laws 11.445/2007 and 14.026/2020 (institutional_fragmentation).
